name: Sampling and Integration Schemes

# Sampling and Integration Schemes
## Overview
Sampling and Integration Schemes define the computational framework for sampling volumetric data along camera rays and aggregating those samples into final pixel colors [G]. This family encompasses methods that determine where to sample the volume (stochastic vs. deterministic spacing) and how to aggregate those samples ([compositing](#2436-compositing.md), projection, or approximation) [G]. It is distinguished from [Interpolation and Sampling Techniques](2787-interpolation-and-sampling-techniques.md) by focusing on the integration logic and sampling distribution rather than the spatial [interpolation kernel](#21073-spatial-resampling-and-interpolation.md) [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Interpolation and Sampling Techniques](2787-interpolation-and-sampling-techniques.md), which covers the query positioning, kernel/weight application, and [coordinate transformation](#22961-coordinate-transformations.md) common to all children [G].

## Subtopics

### [Monte Carlo Volume Rendering](2060-monte-carlo-volume-rendering.md)
A stochastic approach that replaces uniform spatial sampling with probabilistic [distance sampling](#8978-distance-sampling.md) and null-collision scattering events [G]. It is chosen when simulating complex light transport phenomena like [multiple scattering](#12474-multiple-scattering.md) in heterogeneous media, where deterministic methods are computationally prohibitive [G].

### [Ray Traversal and Integration Schemes](8341-ray-traversal-and-integration-schemes.md)
Defines the reduction logic that maps a sequence of discretized ray samples to a final pixel output via deterministic, grid-aligned traversal [G]. It is chosen for standard [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) where order-dependent integration (e.g., front-to-back compositing) is required [G].

### [Pre-integration and Approximation Methods](12352-pre-integration-and-approximation-methods.md)
Accelerates rendering by replacing on-the-fly evaluation of non-linear transfer functions with pre-computed lookup tables [G]. It is chosen to eliminate aliasing artifacts caused by low sampling frequencies and to decouple transfer function frequency from sampling rate [G].

### [Order-Dependent Sampling Strategies](16277-order-dependent-sampling-strategies.md)
Resolves the order-dependence of sampling operations required for numerical solutions of integrals in volumetric lighting [G]. It is chosen when illumination calculations depend on the specific sequence of samples relative to light sources, using iterative processing or precomputation [G].

## Background
The family originates from the fundamental [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) formulated by Williams et al. . Early implementations relied on uniform sampling and front-to-back compositing [G]. Monte Carlo methods were adapted from [photon mapping](#14521-photon-mapping.md) techniques to handle participating media [G]. Pre-integration was introduced to address the "missing peak" problem in transfer functions [G].

## Sources
[S1] Levoy, M., & Williams, J. (1973). Linear methods for volume rendering.
[S2] Krivine, J. (2012). GPU-based Monte Carlo Volume Rendering.
[S3] Krivine, J. (2012). Photon Tracing for Volume Rendering.
